purpose: Evaluate source-backed named Go struct-field declaration coverage and unexpected additions across every tracked Go file in the pinned Litestream repository, using one Go standard-library parser oracle and the frozen graphs.
developmentStatus: The selected two-file 33-field result and candidate graph were inspected before this full-repository registration. This is broader development qualification, not an unseen holdout.
sourceFiles: All tracked paths ending in .go from git ls-files, including tests and generated files; no post-hoc file exclusions.
sourceOracle: Go standard-library go/parser and go/ast; include top-level named StructType TypeSpecs and each explicit Field.Names identifier except the blank identifier. Keep embedded and blank fields separate. Exclude anonymous nested struct fields from the outer direct-member denominator. Preserve full repository-relative file path and exact 1-based identifier line.
join: Use the same exact source file, owner name/start line, field name/identifier line and source-owner-to-target-field contains/defines record rule as go_struct_field_registration.json. Require a distinct field declaration node for each source identifier. Do not credit field-type context references as declarations. Report missing or ambiguous owner and field identities separately. Candidate graph additions require a matching source field under this rule; inspect every added field node and its owner.
report: Retain all source declarations and per-graph exact/ambiguous/missing statuses, every unexpected candidate field node, unchanged baseline node/edge checks, source/graph/binary hashes, diagnostics and unavailable outcomes. Separate declaration coverage from field-access correctness and god-object diagnosis.
limitations: One known Go development repository cannot establish cross-language extraction quality or broad superiority.
Publication exclusions and parser recovery remain visible; source fields in excluded files count as unavailable or missing rather than disappearing from the denominator.
A matching declaration identity does not prove field-access target precision, cohesion, responsibility count or user-facing explanation quality.
